chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who placed a thousand dirhams for his dependents as expense money, and a year passed upon it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was staying, it is subject to Zakat, and if he was absent, it is not subject to Zakat.'

key_terms.حَالَ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ: A lunar year passed upon it

ai.seo_question: Does Zakat apply to money saved for family expenses if the owner is traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of 'presence' (hudur) in the location of wealth for Zakat liability, distinguishing between a resident owner who remains subject to the obligation and an absent owner who is exempt. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that physical presence in the place where the Nisab is held is a prerequisite for the lunar year (hawl) to complete and trigger the duty. This ruling underscores the practical application of Zakat laws regarding movable wealth intended for family sustenance.
